key_highlights: Iron ore prices crumble, pressuring BHP and major miners; BHP under severe strategic stress
Energy stocks lift ASX on rising oil prices amid tanker-war tensions
Australian housing price falls accelerate dramatically; RBA signals no rescue intervention
EV sales outpace petrol cars for first time in Australia; BYD declares EV tipping point reached
Bathla construction collapse (213 staff stood down) signals broader construction sector fragility
Small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar) lead ASX momentum
US midterm uncertainty and Trump policy threats add global risk premium
Australians driven to second jobs as mortgage costs bite; consumer sentiment deteriorating

sectors.trend: Iron ore in freefall pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX; however small-cap gold (AUR.AX) and critical minerals (vanadium, rare earths) outperform on supply-chain and AI-infrastructure demand
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners face margin compression; rotate into small-cap gold and critical-mineral names (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals)

sectors.trend: Oil rises on tanker-war tensions; energy stocks provide ASX support. Tanker disruptions unlikely to suppress supply long-term but create volatility
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, and upstream producers benefit from price spikes; monitor LNG contract pricing for BHP.AX and Santos exposure

sectors.trend: Accelerating housing price falls and rising mortgage stress (second jobs) threaten NIM and credit quality; RBA explicitly rules out property rescue
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face rising NPL risk; REITs (VGP.AX, DGL.AX) under pressure from falling valuations and higher discount rates

sectors.trend: EV sales surpass petrol cars for first time; BYD declares Australia past tipping point. Consumer squeeze from mortgage costs drives cost-conscious spending
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WTW.AX face margin pressure; EV infrastructure and charging names gain; VW global job cuts (50,000) signal auto-sector distress

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse (213 staff, funding extension) is a bellwether for broader construction fragility; tradie skills shortage persists
sectors.implications: WTC.AX, WES.AX (building division) and construction-linked REITs face project-delivery risk; government tradie qualification scheme may ease supply

sectors.trend: Global AI capex boom (Nvidia, Broadcom, Snowflake, Adobe) continues; Australia's defence drone procurement and Raytheon contracts signal structural spend shift
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX tech exposure; monitor CSL.AX (health-tech) and any ASX-listed defence/drone plays; global AI sentiment supports risk appetite

key_themes: Commodity bifurcation: iron ore weakness vs. gold/critical-minerals strength
Housing correction accelerates with no RBA backstop
EV transition inflection point in Australia
US political risk (midterms, Trump threats) elevating global volatility
Consumer squeeze: mortgage stress, second jobs, cost-of-living pressure
Defence spending structural shift toward drones

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce large-cap miner exposure; hedge via small-cap gold and critical-mineral rotation

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Housing market acceleration of falls / credit event
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight banks and property REITs; monitor NAB.AX, ANZ.AX NPL pipelines; RBA unlikely to intervene

risk_assessment.risk_factor: US political / trade policy shock (Trump threats, midterms)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain AUD hedges; diversify away from US-listed exposure; monitor AUD/USD for risk-off spikes
Screen construction-linked ASX names for funding runway; favour government-backed projects
Favour defensive staples (WES.AX, WTW.AX) over discretionary; monitor retail sales data

risk_assessment.risk_factor: El Niño / climate disruption to agriculture and energy
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor SUG.AX, TNL.AX crop exposure; energy demand spikes from extreme weather

opportunities.recommendation: Rotate from large-cap iron ore miners into small-cap gold and critical-mineral explorers
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore in structural downtrend; gold and vanadium/rare-earth names benefiting from AI-infrastructure and supply-chain diversification demand

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy exposure on oil price spike from tanker tensions
opportunities.rationale: Tanker wars support near-term oil prices; upstream producers benefit from volatility premium

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight defensive consumer staples amid consumer squeeze
opportunities.rationale: Mortgage stress and second-job trend compress discretionary spend; staples offer resilience

opportunities.recommendation: Monitor EV-infrastructure and charging ASX plays
opportunities.rationale: EV sales surpassing petrol cars marks structural inflection; BYD tipping-point declaration accelerates adoption

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce or hedge bank and property REIT exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Accelerating housing falls with no RBA rescue raise NPL risk and cap-fall risk; RBA explicitly rules out intervention

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim large-cap iron ore miner positions
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore 'crumbling' signals sustained margin pressure; BHP strategic uncertainty elevates idiosyncratic risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain AUD/USD hedge and cash buffer for US political volatility
defensive_moves.rationale: Trump threats and midterm uncertainty could trigger risk-off AUD selloff; construction contagion adds domestic risk

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely under pressure: iron ore weakness drags materials, housing falls weigh on financials/REITs. Energy provides partial offset. Small-cap miners and gold offer relative strength. Expect choppy, risk-off bias into US midterms.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural shift toward critical minerals, EV infrastructure, and AI-linked supply chains supports selective ASX upside. Housing correction may extend 6–12 months absent RBA intervention. Consumer squeeze persists through 2026. Defence and drone procurement offer a multi-year tailwind.
